one_liner: 128-bit AES-NI bulk hash for x86-64 file and asset hashing; about 3x XXH64's large-buffer throughput, roughly tied with XXH3.
what_it_does: Meow is a single C/C++ header (meow_hash_x64_aesni.h) that hashes a buffer of any length into a 128-bit __m128i. It was built for change detection and deduplication in a game asset pipeline where SHA-1 was too slow. You call MeowHash(seed, len, ptr) with a 128-byte seed (MeowDefaultSeed, or one derived with MeowExpandSeed). A streaming API (MeowBegin/MeowAbsorb/MeowEnd) gives the same result, and MeowU64From/MeowU32From truncate the output. The interface does not match xxHash: there is no integer seed, the output is a SIMD register rather than a uint64_t, and v0.5 has no portable C fallback.
how_it_is_fast: There are eight 128-bit accumulator lanes. Each 32-byte chunk drives two AES decryption rounds (aesdec) on two lanes, plus 64-bit adds and XORs into others of the same data reloaded at 1-byte offsets. The main loop consumes 256 bytes per iteration, which the authors describe as 16 AES rounds per 256 bytes, with a design target of 16 bytes/cycle. Above about 256 KB (0x3ff blocks) the loop switches to a variant with explicit prefetcht0 4 KB ahead. Tail bytes are fetched with one unaligned 16-byte load plus a pshufb/pand mask, which may read past the end of the buffer but never crosses a page. Finalisation is a fixed 12-step AES/add/xor shuffle that folds eight lanes into one, so every input under 32 bytes costs about the same (about 61 cycles).
when_to_use: Change detection, deduplication and cache keys for large files or assets (tens of KB to GB) on x86-64 CPUs with AES-NI. SMHasher3 measures about 12.4 bytes/cycle at 256 KB, against 4.0 for XXH64 and 7.0 for wyhash.

Cases that need a full 128-bit hash of data you control, where accidental collisions must be negligible. Meow passes all 250 SMHasher3 tests at 32, 64 and 128 bits, while XXH3-128 fails 36 and AquaHash fails 55 in the same summary.
Replacing SHA-1 or MD5 used purely as a content fingerprint in a trusted build or asset pipeline, where there is no adversary.
Codebases that can vendor one zlib-licensed header and already compile with -maes -mssse3 (or MSVC on x64).
when_not_to_use: Hash-table keys or anything under about 64 bytes. SMHasher3 puts Meow at about 61.5 cycles/hash for 1-32 byte keys, against 29.3 for wyhash and 30.7 for XXH3-64.

Any adversarial setting: MACs, hash-flooding-resistant tables, or content addressing an attacker can influence. Peter Schmidt-Nielsen's 2021 cryptanalysis found a key-independent differential with probability about 2^-45, key recovery in about 2^49 queries, and SAT-built full 128-bit collisions for a known key (issue #80). The README downgraded v0.5 to 'level 1' and points to SipHash.
Non-x86 targets, CPUs without AES-NI, or code that needs runtime dispatch. v0.5 ships only the x64 AES-NI header, with no ARM, C or runtime-detection path (issue #86 is still open).

Projects that want a maintained dependency with a stable spec. v0.5 is still labelled a 'proposal' and never reached v1.0. The last code change was in 2021, and the NoHatCoder 0.6 candidates (#82) were never merged.

Plain bulk speed on modern x86 where XXH3 is an option. xxHash's own benchmark (i7-9700K, clang 10, -O3 -mavx2) has XXH3-AVX2 at 59.4 GB/s against Meow at 58.2 GB/s, and SMHasher3 has XXH3-64 at 12.82 against Meow's 12.43 bytes/cycle, with XXH3 about 2x faster on small inputs.

integration.min_toolchain: C or C++ compiler with AES-NI and SSSE3/SSE4.1 intrinsics; build scripts use clang++ -O3 -maes -mavx (or -msse4) and MSVC cl -O2. GCC needs -maes -mssse3 at minimum or it fails with 'inlining failed ... target specific option mismatch' (#70). No minimum version is documented.
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AES-NI (32-bit x86 compiles but is untested, and MeowU64From is broken there, #74); Windows/MSVC, Windows/clang, Linux/clang per README; no ARM or portable fallback in v0.5
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. MeowHash is a pure function of its arguments with no global mutable state (unless MEOW_DUMP is defined); the streaming meow_state is per-caller.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it can replace XXH64/CityHash64 as a content fingerprint if you store MeowU64From(hash, 0) or the full 128 bits, but the API (128-byte seed, __m128i result) and the hash values differ, and it is not a suitable std::hash / hash-table replacement.

gotchas: Reads up to 15 bytes past the end of the input (without crossing a 4 KB page) and masks them off. ASan reports this as global-buffer-overflow (#79, closed as 'not a buffer overflow'); the PR to add an ASan guard (#83) is unmerged, so exclude the function from ASan yourself.
The input and seed parameters are non-const void* (a const PR was merged and then reverted, #71/#72; #78 is open), so C++ callers must cast away const.

Hash values changed between v0.2, v0.3, v0.4 and v0.5, and the archived mollyrocket.com/meowhash docs describe the older API (meow_intrinsics.h, MeowHash_Accelerated, an ARM and C version) that is not in the v0.5 header. The live site is gone (#87), and the .travis.yml still references the removed headers.
MeowU64From/MeowU32From require a compile-time-constant lane index (_mm_extract_epi64); on 32-bit builds the macro ignores the index and always returns the low 64 bits (#74, open).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose Meow over xxHash (XXH3/XXH128) or AquaHash when you hash large trusted buffers on x86-64 with AES-NI and want a 128-bit result that passes every SMHasher3 test; XXH3 matches its bulk speed but fails 27-36 SMHasher3 tests, and AquaHash is faster in bulk (15.84 bytes/cycle) but fails 55. Choose wyhash, rapidhash or a5hash for short keys and hash tables, and xxHash when you need portability, an integer seed or an actively maintained library.
verified_claims_summary: SMHasher3 measured the bulk speed of its lightly modified MeowHash copy single-threaded on 262,017-262,144-byte keys at random alignment: 12.43 bytes/cycle (40.5 GiB/s at a nominal 3.5 GHz), against XXH-64 3.99, CityHash-64 4.75, wyhash 6.98 and XXH3-64 12.82. The copy is identical to upstream at seed 0 and adds a 64-bit seed in the nonce slot; CPU model and compiler are not named. Separately, xxHash's wiki (i7-9700K, clang 10, -O3 -mavx2) has Meow at 58.2 GB/s, about 3x XXH64's 19.4 GB/s and level with XXH3-AVX2's 59.4 GB/s.
status_note: Abandoned: the last commit (2021-07-02) only added the security notice, and v0.5 never left 'proposal' status. It is zlib-licensed, a single 744-line header that is easy to vendor, has 1.8k stars and 22 open issues, and is not archived.
